description: Defines gap categories, priority scoring, discoverability levels, and interview question templates for knowledge gaps identified during research

product_coverage.description: Gaps in understanding which product lines use CDM
product_coverage.discoverability_rationale: Banks rarely disclose product-level technology details publicly

jurisdiction.description: Gaps in understanding regulatory jurisdiction priorities and rollout
jurisdiction.discoverability_rationale: Some regulatory compliance info public, but CDM-specific approach rarely disclosed

vendor.description: Gaps in understanding vendor relationships and build vs buy decisions
vendor.discoverability_rationale: Vendor relationships rarely disclosed; competitive sensitivity

driver.description: Gaps in understanding adoption pressures and hesitations
driver.discoverability_rationale: Some signals from regulatory filings and tech investments

counterparty.description: Gaps in understanding counterparty CDM readiness and interoperability
counterparty.discoverability_rationale: Bilateral relationships confidential; some CCP info public

strategic.description: Gaps in understanding future CDM roadmap and competitive positioning
strategic.discoverability_rationale: Strategic plans confidential; rarely disclosed publicly

technical.description: Gaps in understanding technical implementation details
technical.discoverability_rationale: Some signals from job postings and conference talks

very_low.description: Almost never available from public sources
very_low.resolution_approach: Requires insider interview or direct relationship

low.resolution_approach: May require conference networking or vendor back-channel

low_medium.resolution_approach: Extended web research, regulatory filings, industry analyst reports

medium.resolution_approach: Standard web search, trade press, public filings

business_impact.description: How much does resolving this gap affect the usefulness of the assessment?

resolution_value.description: How much would resolving this gap improve confidence or change classification?

discoverability_penalty.description: Higher penalty = harder to discover = more valuable if resolved

strategic_urgency.description: How time-sensitive is resolving this gap?

interview_question_bank.description: Three-tier question framework: Tier 1 (opening/rapport), Tier 2 (probing), Tier 3 (specific/detailed)

tier1_opening: How would you describe your firm's approach to regulatory reporting technology across different asset classes?
Which product lines have been the focus of your recent regulatory reporting investments?
How do you think about standardization versus customization across your derivatives business?
tier2_probing: For [IRS/CDS/FX], what's driving your technology approach for EMIR Refit compliance?
Are you seeing different adoption patterns for CDM across rates versus credit products?
How does your approach differ between high-volume products like IRS and more complex structured products?
tier3_specific: What percentage of your [product] trades currently flow through CDM-based workflows?
For which specific products are you using CDM in production versus pilot?
What's your target CDM coverage across asset classes by end of 2025?

tier1_opening: How are you prioritizing the various global regulatory reporting deadlines?
Which regulatory change is driving the most technology investment for you right now?
How do you balance global consistency with local regulatory requirements?
tier2_probing: After EMIR Refit, what's your approach for the CFTC rewrite deadline?
How are you thinking about the JSCC CDM requirement for June 2025?
Do you plan to use the same technology approach across EU, UK, and US, or different solutions?
tier3_specific: Which jurisdiction was your first CDM deployment, and what's the planned sequence for others?
Are you using CDM for your EMIR Refit reporting, or a traditional approach?
What's your timeline for extending CDM to non-EU jurisdictions?

tier1_opening: How do you think about build versus buy for regulatory reporting technology?
What role do vendors play in your derivatives technology strategy?
How important is internal capability building versus leveraging vendor solutions?
tier2_probing: For CDM specifically, are you building internal expertise or relying on vendor implementations?
How do you evaluate CDM vendors versus building your own CDM layer?
What's your experience with vendors like [Delta Capita/Murex/Calypso] for CDM implementation?
tier3_specific: Which vendor(s) are you using for CDM implementation, and for which products?
What's the split between internal development and vendor-provided CDM components?
Do you have an internal CDM team, or is it entirely outsourced to vendors?

tier1_opening: What's driving your technology investments in derivatives operations right now?
How do you prioritize regulatory compliance versus operational efficiency improvements?
What are the biggest challenges you're facing in derivatives technology?
tier2_probing: Beyond regulatory deadlines, what business drivers are pushing CDM adoption?
What factors might slow down or delay your CDM implementation?
How does M&A integration or other organizational changes affect your CDM plans?
tier3_specific: Is regulatory compliance the primary driver, or are you seeing efficiency benefits that justify CDM investment?
What capacity constraints or competing priorities are affecting your CDM timeline?
What would need to change for you to accelerate CDM adoption?

tier1_opening: How are you thinking about connectivity with counterparties on regulatory reporting?
What's your experience with CCP connectivity requirements like JSCC's CDM mandate?
How do you coordinate technology standards with your major trading counterparties?
tier2_probing: Are you seeing pressure from major dealers or CCPs to adopt CDM?
How does counterparty CDM readiness affect your interoperability planning?
What's your approach to utilities like Delta Capita or DTCC for CDM connectivity?
tier3_specific: Which of your major counterparties are CDM-enabled, and how does that affect your approach?
Are you planning bilateral CDM connectivity with specific dealers?
What's your CCP CDM connectivity status with LCH, CME, and JSCC?

tier1_opening: How do you see regulatory reporting technology evolving over the next 3-5 years?
What's your long-term vision for derivatives technology standardization?
How important is being an early mover versus fast follower in regulatory technology?
tier2_probing: Do you see CDM as a strategic differentiator or table stakes?
How does CDM fit into your broader derivatives technology strategy?
What would need to happen for CDM to become your primary data model for derivatives?
tier3_specific: What's your 2025-2027 CDM roadmap?
Are you planning to contribute to CDM open-source development or primarily consume?
What budget allocation do you have for CDM implementation?

tier1_opening: How would you describe your derivatives technology architecture?
What's your approach to data standardization across trading systems?
How do you think about integrating new data standards into existing infrastructure?
tier2_probing: Where does CDM fit in your technology stack - at the edge or in the core?
Are you adopting CDM as a translation layer or native data model?
What's your experience with CDM's Java/Python/JSON representations?
tier3_specific: What's your CDM implementation architecture - event sourcing, microservices, monolith?
Which CDM version are you targeting, and how do you handle version upgrades?
Do you have a dedicated CDM team, and what's the team structure?

counterparty_pressure.description: Trading partners requiring or preferring CDM

competitive_positioning.description: Strategic desire to lead in technology adoption

operational_efficiency.description: Business case for cost savings or efficiency

vendor_preference.description: Preference for vendor solution over internal CDM build

wait_for_maturity.description: Waiting for CDM standard or ecosystem to mature

net_assessment_framework.description: Framework for assessing balance of pressures vs hesitations
